webpack puts the target of each `import()` in its own file. Without a `webpackChunkName` comment, a production build names that file with a number, such as `472.js`, which tells you nothing in a network tab or a bundle report.

The comment goes inside the parentheses, before the path. It must be a block comment with one space after `/*` and one before `*/`. An import with `webpackMode: "eager"` doesn't make a chunk, so it doesn't need a name, and giving it one is reported too.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"import/dynamic-import-chunkname" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default. The ones that are commented out are unset by default.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"import/dynamic-import-chunkname" = ["error", {
  importFunctions = [], # list of strings
  allowEmpty = false,
  # webpackChunknameFormat = <string>,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
const settings = await import("./pages/settings.js");
```

{/* bad */}
```js
const settings = await import(
  // webpackChunkName: "settings"
  "./pages/settings.js"
);
```

{/* bad */}
```js
const settings = await import(/*webpackChunkName: "settings"*/ "./pages/settings.js");
```

{/* bad */}
```js
const settings = await import(
  /* webpackChunkName: "settings", webpackMode: "eager" */
  "./pages/settings.js"
);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const settings = await import(/* webpackChunkName: "settings" */ "./pages/settings.js");

const admin = await import(
  /* webpackChunkName: "admin", webpackPrefetch: true */
  "./pages/admin.js"
);

const icons = await import(/* webpackMode: "eager" */ "./icons.js");
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `importFunctions` | `[]` | Names of functions that are checked like `import()`. |
| `allowEmpty` | `false` | Allow an import without a chunk name. A malformed comment is still reported. |
| `webpackChunknameFormat` | `"([0-9a-zA-Z-_/.]\|\[(request\|index)\])+"` | A regular expression that the chunk name must match. |

{/* bad {"options": [{"importFunctions": ["lazyLoad"]}]} */}
```js
const settings = lazyLoad("./pages/settings.js");
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allowEmpty": true}]} */}
```js
const settings = await import("./pages/settings.js");
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"allowEmpty": true}]} */}
```js
const settings = await import(/*webpackPrefetch: true*/ "./pages/settings.js");
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"webpackChunknameFormat": "page-[a-z]+"}]} */}
```js
const settings = await import(/* webpackChunkName: "settings" */ "./pages/settings.js");
```

{/* good {"options": [{"webpackChunknameFormat": "page-[a-z]+"}]} */}
```js
const settings = await import(/* webpackChunkName: "page-settings" */ "./pages/settings.js");
```

## When not to use it

The comment only matters to webpack and to bundlers that read webpack's comments. If you bundle with `bun build`, leave this rule off.
